title: O’Neal to Host Shredding Event at Hollywood Casino

O’Neal to Host Shredding Event at Hollywood Casino
April 13, 2026
HARRISBURG
– As a free service to the community, Rep. Tim O’Neal (R-Washington) will be holding a shredding event on Saturday, April 18, at Hollywood Casino at the Meadows to give residents of the 48th Legislative District a chance to safeguard themselves against identity theft by having their personal documents securely destroyed.
The event will be held from 9-11 a.m. at
210 Racetrack Road, Washington
.
“Identity theft continues to be a serious issue,” O’Neal said. “Thieves can obtain personal information in many ways, but one of the easiest ways to protect yourself is by securely disposing of documents that contain sensitive data. I encourage all residents to take part in this event.”
Acceptable items include all paper documents. No more than three brown paper grocery bags or open small cardboard boxes per household are permitted, and no businesses, please. Bags are preferred to boxes. In addition, no large binder clips or hardbound covers will be accepted. Materials more than 1-inch thick will need to be broken down.
All items to be shredded are to be placed in the trunk of the vehicle, and participants should not get out of their vehicle in order to speed the process. Once a person arrives at the event, he or she should open their trunk.
For more information, contact O’Neal’s Washington district office at 724-223-4541.
The 48th Legislative District in Washington County covers the city of Washington; Amwell, part of Carroll (Districts 3, 4 and 5), East Finley, Fallowfield, Morris, North Franklin, part of North Strabane (Districts 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5), Nottingham, Somerset, South Franklin, South Strabane, and West Finley townships; and the boroughs of Donora, East Washington and Green Hills.

O’Neal to Hold Property Tax/Rent Rebate Clinics
March 4, 2026
HARRISBURG – Rep. Tim O’Neal (R-Washington) today announced his office will host two Property Tax/Rent Rebate Clinics during the month of March.
“No one should pay for assistance in completing the program’s application,” O’Neal said. “I’m pleased to be able to have my staff out in the community to make it easier to apply.”
The clinics will be:
•	Tuesday, March 10, at the Claysville Community Center, 212 Main St., Claysville, from 10 a.m. to noon in partnership with Rep. Josh Kail (R-Beaver/Washington).
•	Tuesday, March 17, at the Donora Senior Center, 683 Meldon Ave., Donora, from 9:30 a.m. to 1 p.m.

Assistance completing the application will be offered on a first-come, first-served basis. Please bring identification, all proof of 2025 income, and a signed rent certificate or paid property tax receipts.

title: House Republican Leaders Respond to Shapiro Budget Proposal
raw_text:
House Republican Leaders Respond to Shapiro Budget Proposal
February 3, 2026
HARRISBURG – Leaders of the Pennsylvania House Republican Caucus Tuesday responded to Gov. Josh Shapiro’s Fiscal Year 2026-27 budget proposal with the following comments:
House Republican Leader Jesse Topper (R-Bedford/Fulton):
“As with past budget proposals from this administration, the product unveiled today spends too much, grows government too much and relies too much on unsustainable sources of revenue. I am also deeply concerned about the illegitimate use of the Rainy Day Fund to create a $100 million slush fund that obscures the lines of federalism.
“Our number one priority must be providing the foundation for substantial economic growth in the Commonwealth to balance any future state budgets. We also must begin—right now—the hard work of reducing the size and scope of government so we do not continue to take too much from hardworking Pennsylvania taxpayers who are already struggling to make ends meet.”
House Republican Whip Tim O’Neal (R-Washington):
“The affordability crisis is real and people are struggling. This proposal by Gov. Shapiro is irresponsible and will contribute to rising costs across the state. We cannot continue to rely on new taxes and accounting tricks to fill in the gaps. The only way to raise revenue without digging deeper into the pockets of Pennsylvanians is to inject new life into our state’s economy. Get government out of the way by making it easier for people to save money, get to work and earn in Pennsylvania.”
House Republican Appropriations Committee Chairman Jim Struzzi (R-Indiana):
“The governor’s proposal today is just the start of the budget process. This $53.26 billion budget is an increase of $2.72 billion, or 5.4%, over the current fiscal year. I have major concerns not just on the spending side, but also on the revenue proposals and fiscal solvency of the Commonwealth in future years. I look forward to our three weeks of budget hearings to review this budget line-by-line and work toward a comprise budget that meets the needs of all Pennsylvanians.”
Republican Leader Jesse Topper

title: Grow the Economy Instead of Taxes, O’Neal Says
raw_text:
Grow the Economy Instead of Taxes, O’Neal Says
February 3, 2026
HARRISBURG – Rep. Tim O’Neal (R-Washington) today issued the following statement in response to Gov. Josh Shapiro’s $53.26 billion Fiscal Year 2026-27 budget proposal:
“I feel like a broken record. The affordability crisis is real and people are struggling. This proposal by Gov. Shapiro is irresponsible and will contribute to rising costs across the state. We cannot continue to rely on new taxes and accounting tricks to fill in the gaps. The only way to raise revenue without digging deeper into the pockets of Pennsylvanians is to inject new life into our state’s economy. Get government out of the way by making it easier for people to save money, get to work and earn in Pennsylvania. When the economy grows, so does state revenue. We do this by leveraging Pennsylvania’s greatest economic strength – our energy sector.
“Pennsylvanians has an abundance of natural gas under our feet. It is the most affordable and reliable source of energy. We should be embracing it, not shunning it. Despite interest from major companies in constructing a multi-billion-dollar liquified natural gas facility in Philadelphia, building and permitting regulations have stood in the way. A facility like this would result in billions of dollars in statewide economic investment and create ripple effects such as creating thousands of new jobs.”
“Now is the time to be focusing on permitting reform instead of deliberately undermining our energy producers through ideologically driven regulations. Unleashing our energy potential will not only lower energy bills but will also address a looming energy crisis.”

Grants Awarded for Projects in 48th District, O’Neal Says
January 20, 2026
HARRISBURG – Rep. Tim O’Neal (R-Washington) today announced almost $2.1 million in grants from the Commonwealth Financing Authority (CFA) were awarded for projects throughout the 48th Legislative District under two programs.
“These grants address pressing storm water and transportation issues in the 48th Legislative District,” O’Neal said. “By tackling stormwater problems, erosion and flooding are reduced. In addition, fixing roadways reduces wear and tear on vehicles, thus mitigating costs for drivers. I will continue to advocate for funds for Washington County.”
The Multimodal Transportation Fund (MTF) provides grants to encourage economic development and ensure a safe and reliable system of transportation is available in the Commonwealth. Those receiving MTF grants are:
•	Amwell Township – $169,700 to replace the East Hillsboro Road Bridge.
•	Carroll Township – $339,850 to remediate a landslide along Columbia Road.
•	North Franklin Chestnut LLC – $650,056 to repave the outer ring road at the Washington Crown Center.
The Pennsylvania Small Water and Sewer Program awards grants to assist with the construction, improvement, expansion, or rehabilitation or repair of a water supply system, sanitary sewer system, storm sewer system or flood control project. Those receiving these grants are:
•	Carroll Township – $73,312 to construct a bioswale for stormwater at Valley Avenue Park.
•	Carroll Township Authority – $260,525 to upgrade the Pigeon Creek Pump Station.
•	North Strabane Township – $50,073 to fix uncontrolled runoff near McGregor Avenue to address erosion and the flow velocity of generated runoff.
•	North Strabane Township – $116,090 for a drainage improvement project along Curry Avenue to prevent shoulder collapse.
•	Washington-East Washington Joint Authority – $425,000 to rehabilitate manholes along the Chartiers Interceptor Sewer, which conveys stormwater from seven different municipalities.

O’Neal Joins House Leadership in Calling for Investigation into School District of Philadelphia for Discrimination
September 29, 2026
HARRISBURG – Rep. Tim O’Neal (R-Washington), Republican whip, today joined other members of House Republican leadership in penning a letter to Attorney General Dave Sunday calling for his office to investigate the School District of Philadelphia (SDP) for discrimination against Jewish students.
“All children should have equal access to education,” O’Neal said. “The reports of alleged behavior by teachers and administrators are alarming. Antisemitism has no place in our society but especially in the classroom. All students should have a safe learning environment and not feel uncomfortable due to their race or religion.”
The letter asks Sunday to have his Civil Rights Enforcement Section investigate whether a systemic pattern of discrimination against Jewish students exists in the SDP that consequently prevents these students from equal access to education. In addition, the letter asks Sunday’s office to determine if potential violations of the Pennsylvania Crimes Code have occurred in the SDP, including, but not limited to, ethnic intimidation and harassment.
In 2025, the chairman of the U.S. House of Representatives’ Education and Workforce Committee launched an investigation into three school districts, including SDP, after receiving reports of Jewish students being harassed and subjected to open antisemitism in classrooms and hallways. A year earlier, SDP settled a federal discrimination case with the U.S. Department of Education after students allegedly taunted Jewish classmates. Despite this settlement, a video circulated in 2025 shows an SDP administrator blaming Israel for the Oct. 7, 2023, massacre of Israeli civilians. In addition, teachers in the school district have been using pro-Palestinian materials.
“It’s obvious the School District of Philadelphia is not taking antisemitism seriously,” O’Neal added. “Parents have even complained to Gov. Josh Shapiro to no avail. I encourage the attorney general to use his resources to ensure a safe learning environment for all.”

“Finally, this budget reins in out-of-control government spending. By reforming our public benefit systems, we can ensure that help is going to the Pennsylvanians that need it the most.”

title: O’Neal, Anderson, Rader, Warner, Flood Unveil Common-Sense, Six-Bill Property Tax Reform Package
raw_text:
O’Neal, Anderson, Rader, Warner, Flood Unveil Common-Sense, Six-Bill Property Tax Reform Package
October 15, 2026
HARRISBURG
– Rep. Tim O’Neal (R-Washington) today announced he is spearheading a six-bill legislative package aimed at addressing Pennsylvania’s growing property tax burden, improving school district accountability and giving homeowners greater control over the taxes they pay.
Four other colleagues from across the state have joined him in introducing these bills: Reps. Marc Anderson (R-York), Jack Rader (R-Monroe), Ryan Warner (R-Fayette) and Ann Flood (R-Northampton).
“For too many Pennsylvanians, the cost of owning a home has become increasingly unpredictable,” said Anderson. “Families are already struggling with the rising costs of groceries, utilities and everyday necessities. The last thing they need is another unexpected property tax increase making it harder to afford their homes.”
“Whether you’re a young family purchasing your first home or a retiree who has spent decades paying off a mortgage, you deserve to know that your home will remain affordable,” Warner said. “Property taxes shouldn’t be a moving target that homeowners have no control over.”
“Pennsylvanians shouldn’t have to worry that a single vote at a sparsely attended school board meeting could make their homes less affordable,” Rader said. “These proposals are about restoring predictability, demanding accountability and ensuring that taxpayers have a meaningful voice in decisions affecting their household budgets.”
“Counties shouldn’t be able to kick the can down the road with years of zero property tax increases and then a sudden 43.5% increase like just proposed in Northampton County, or Allegheny County’s 36% increase in 2025, or Dauphin County’s 21.8% increase in 2025,” said Flood. “It’s bad government, and my legislation will bring some much-needed predictability and accountability to county budgeting while giving taxpayers the final say when officials want to raise taxes beyond a reasonable limit.”
The legislative package includes six bills designed to provide meaningful relief while strengthening taxpayer protections:
•
Giving Taxpayers a Say in Property Tax Increases (Anderson)
: Requires voter approval before school districts can increase school property taxes over the Act 1 index. This bill would ensure that taxpayers have the final say over extreme increases to their tax bills.
•
Establishing Annual Limits on County Property Tax Increases (Flood)
: Limits annual county property tax rate increases to the lesser of 4% or the applicable regional inflation rate, unless a larger increase is approved by voters through a referendum. The bill would encourage more consistent fiscal planning and protect taxpayers from sudden, substantial tax hikes.
•
Requiring Voter Approval for Major School Construction Debt (Rader)
: Requires school districts to obtain voter approval before borrowing money for major construction and renovation projects, with limited exceptions for emergencies. The bill would provide greater transparency and accountability for long-term spending commitments that can drive property tax increases.
•
Closing Loopholes in School District Borrowing (Flood)
: Prevents school districts from circumventing voter approval requirements through alternative borrowing arrangements. This companion measure for Rader’s bill would ensure taxpayers retain a meaningful voice in major financial decisions, regardless of how a school district structures its debt.
•
Accountability in Education Spending (O’Neal)
: Establishes a formula to rank school districts by student performance on standardized tests against per-student spending. School districts ranking in the bottom half statewide would be required to obtain voter approval before increasing property tax rates. The bill would encourage responsible and targeted spending, while recognizing that taxpayers deserve real results for their investment.
•
Providing Counties with a New Property Tax Relief Option (Warner)
: Allows counties, but only with voter approval, to enact an earned income tax of up to 1%, with all revenue dedicated exclusively to reducing county property taxes on eligible homesteads and farmsteads. This optional approach would give communities the opportunity to reduce the burden on homeowners, particularly seniors, farmers and others living on fixed incomes.
O’Neal acknowledged that the proposals are not intended to replace a broader discussion about Pennsylvania’s property tax system, but emphasized that meaningful and common-sense reforms like these should not be delayed while lawmakers debate greater-encompassing solutions.
“We’ve spent decades talking about property tax reform in Harrisburg, but homeowners are still waiting for relief,” O’Neal said. “We may not be able to solve every problem overnight, but we can take practical steps right now to make property taxes more predictable, protect homeowners from unnecessary increases and help Pennsylvanians afford to stay in the homes they’ve worked so hard to own.”
